newsitem.title: UK: Woolwich members set to vote on conversion.
newsitem.headline: Woolwich members set to vote on conversion.

text.p: Members of Britain's Woolwich Building Society -- one of the country's traditional mortgage lenders -- will vote on Tuesday on whether the mutually-owned group should become a public limited company (Plc).

The Woolwich, Britain's third largest building society, is holding a special general meeting in London at which its members -- its savers and borrowers -- will decide whether to give the go-ahead to the 3.0 billion pound ($4.90 billion) flotation.

If the conversion plans are given the thumbs up, qualifying customers will receive at least 450 shares. Last month the Woolwich said this would be to around 2.57 million people, including qualifying members and pensioners. The average windfall to members is expected to be over 1,200 pounds.
Woolwich is one of four building societies planning stock market flotations during 1997. The others are Britain's biggest mortgage lender, the Halifax, the Alliance & Leicester and Northern Rock.
The Woolwich meeting is due to begin at 1430 GMT and the result of the vote, which will include postal and proxy votes, will be known by about 1630 GMT.
If conversion to bank status and the flotation are approved, the new entity is expected to be called Woolwich Plc. ($1=.6120 Pound)
Sir Brian Jenkins, Woolwich chairman said: "The board is very grateful to have received such an overwhelming approval for these proposals".
